name: How to Compare Solar Quotes in Los Angeles County the Right Way

mainEntity.name: How do I compare solar installation quotes in Los Angeles County beyond just cost per watt?
mainEntity.text: How do I compare solar installation quotes in Los Angeles County beyond just cost per watt?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cost per watt is useful but can be misleading when comparing solar quotes in Los Angeles County. First, normalize system size, annual kWh production, and panel wattage. Two 8 kW systems might have very different projected output depending on orientation, shading, and panel efficiency. Check that each proposal models NEM 3.0 exports correctly and uses the same assumed utility rate inflation. Evaluate equipment tiers: panel brand and warranty (product and performance), inverter type (string, DC optimizers, microinverters), and any batteries or EV chargers. Warranties and monitoring coverage can add long-term value, even at a slightly higher upfront price. Scrutinize labor and workmanship warranty length, roof penetration coverage, and response times. Next, review the scope: are main panel upgrades, structural engineering, permits, and interconnection fees included or listed as allowances? How are potential roof repairs handled? Ask each installer to provide a simple layout and shading analysis for your roof, not generic production estimates. Finally, look at installer track record: years in business, number of installations in your specific city, and recent projects with your utility. Create a simple comparison sheet listing cost per watt, equipment, warranties, included extras, production estimates, and financing terms. This approach helps you identify the proposal with the best long-term value, not just the lowest sticker price.
acceptedAnswer.description: Comparing solar quotes in Los Angeles County requires looking beyond cost per watt to evaluate equipment brands, warranties, projected annual production, NEM 3.0 modeling, roof layout, adders like batteries or main panel upgrades, and the installer’s local permitting and utility experience. A structured apples-to-apples comparison spreadsheet is essential.
